objectives.text: The project is titled 'Fraud Detection and Prevention with AI' and is associated with the HawkEye Platform.
The project's funding goal was $19,065.
The project's funding was unsuccessful as the goal was not reached by April 1, 2021.
Global losses from payment fraud tripled from $9.84 billion in 2011 to $32.39 billion in 2020.
The United States accounts for more than one third of global losses from payment fraud.
The online share of total worldwide retail sales reached well over $4 trillion in 2020.
A TransUnion survey found that 22% of Americans experienced fraud during the COVID-19 crisis.
A recent TransUnion survey found that 22% of Americans have been targeted by fraud scams related to COVID-19.

Juniper Research forecasts that businesses in eCommerce, airline ticketing, money transfer, and banking services will cumulatively lose over $200 billion to online payment fraud between 2020 and 2024.

The HawkEye Rule Engine monitors various dimensions pertaining to payments, such as payment amount and frequency of declined authorization attempts.
Clients can connect to the HawkEye Platform using REST API for easy integration into their information systems.
The omnichannel approach of the platform increases its efficiency and versatility in combating online payment fraud.
The HawkEye Platform is designed to increase efficiency and versatility in combating online payment fraud.
The solution is suitable for both merchants processing large volumes of transactions and those operating on a smaller scale.
A 7-day free trial is offered to customers to experience the benefits of the service before payment.
The goal of the campaign is to raise CA$27,000.

innovation.text: HawkEye Risk Solutions utilizes Artificial Intelligence and Data Science to fight fraud.
The HawkEye Platform incorporates multiple AI tools and decision layers to analyze transaction flows holistically.
The HawkEye Rule Engine monitors various dimensions pertaining to payments, such as payment amount and frequency of declined authorization attempts.
The second layer of the HawkEye Platform uses a fully connected Deep Neural Network (DNN) to classify transactions as fraud or not fraud.
The supervised learning model in the HawkEye Platform is trained using the merchant's historical data, where each transaction is labeled as either fraud or non-fraud.
The third layer of the HawkEye Platform is the HawkEye Autoencoder, which attempts to uncover cases of fraud that got past the Rules Engine and Supervised Model.
The HawkEye Autoencoder is trained to create feature representations of valid transactions to detect deviations from the norm.
The team has developed a state-of-the-art fraud detection framework that integrates traditional and modern AI-based methods.
The omnichannel approach of the platform increases its efficiency and versatility in combating online payment fraud.
